stem: A healthy infant has just completed the 6-month preventive health visit. According to the current AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule, when is the next routine well-child visit?
rationale: The 2025 Bright Futures/AAP Periodicity Schedule lists routine preventive visits during infancy at the newborn period, 3-5 days, 1 month, 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, 9 months, and 12 months. Therefore, after the routine 6-month visit, the next scheduled preventive visit for a healthy infant is at 9 months. Additional visits may be needed if health or developmental concerns arise.
educational_objective: Use the AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule to identify the next age-based preventive health visit for a healthy infant.
source_organization: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) / Bright Futures
source_document_title: 2025 Recommendations for Preventive Pediatric Health Care (Periodicity Schedule)
source_version_date: 2025 schedule; interactive schedule last updated 2025-02-07; policy statement published 2025-04-21; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Interactive Periodicity Schedule > Infancy age columns: Newborn, 3-5 days, 1 month, 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, 9 months, 12 months; 2025 policy statement states the schedule remains the current AAP recommendations for preventive pediatric health care
source_claim_supported: The AAP preventive pediatric schedule places the next routine age-based well-child visit after 6 months at 9 months for a healthy infant.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Health Promotion/Disease Prevention and Developmental Stages: provide education about health-promotion recommendations and age-appropriate preventive care, growth, and development

correction_summary: Replaced the vague source item about visits being 'more frequent in infancy' with an exact applied scheduling question based directly on the current AAP Periodicity Schedule. Preserved the healthy-child context and explicitly noted that additional visits may be necessary when concerns exist.
audit_findings: A directly matches the current AAP schedule. B, C, and D are all real later preventive-visit ages, making them plausible distractors, but none is the next scheduled age after 6 months. The stem specifies a healthy infant because AAP notes that children with developmental, psychosocial, chronic disease, or other concerns may need additional visits. No immunization-timing claim is embedded, avoiding confusion with vaccine schedules. Health Promotion and Maintenance is directly supported by NCSBN preventive-care content. One best answer and no unsupported precision remain.
